title: Limits and colimits in total infinity categories of fibrations
statement: Use the infinity-category and smallness conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. An inner fibration is a map of simplicial sets with the right lifting property for all inner horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\subset\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$. A Cartesian fibration is an inner fibration in which each base arrow $b\to p(e)$ has a lift $e'\to e$ such that, for every test object $t$, the square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(t,e')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(t,e)$ and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(t),b)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(t),p(e))$, with vertical maps induced by $p$, is a homotopy pullback. A cocartesian fibration is the opposite notion, with lifts out of an object and the dual mapping-space universal property. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a cocartesian fibration, with fiber $\mathcal E_b$ and transport $f_!:\mathcal E_b\to\mathcal E_{b'}$ for $f:b\to b'$. If the base and all fibers admit small colimits and every $f_!$ preserves small colimits, then $\mathcal E$ admits small colimits. For $a:J\to\mathcal E$, form $b=\operatorname{colim}_J pa$ with cocone maps $f_j:pa(j)\to b$; the colimit of $a$ is the fiber colimit $\operatorname{colim}_j f_{j,!}a(j)\in\mathcal E_b$, equipped with its cocone in $\mathcal E$. Dually, for a Cartesian fibration with complete base and fibers and limit-preserving transports $f^*$, all small limits exist: if $b=\lim_J pa$ with projections $f_j:b\to pa(j)$, then $\lim_Ja=\lim_j f_j^*a(j)$ in $\mathcal E_b$. Both formulas are for small simplicial indexing shapes and homotopy coherent diagrams.

source.place: Lemma 9.8 and its proof via Higher Topos Theory, Corollary 4.3.1.11; opposite-category dual for limits. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Fix a small simplicial set $J$ and a coherent diagram $a:J\to\mathcal E$. Choose a colimiting cocone $\beta:pa\to\Delta_J b$ in the base, using its assumed small colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with $K=J$ and $G=\Delta_J b$. It gives a coherent lift $\lambda:a\to D$ with $D:J\to\mathcal E_b$. Its vertex value is $D(j)=f_{j,!}a(j)$, where $f_j=\beta_j$. Thus the symbols $f_{j,!}a(j)$ form one coherent diagram, not merely a list of objects or maps in a homotopy category. The lifts are applied to this whole transformation; $J$ need not be a nerve.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng-Nikolaus, Lax colimits and free fibrations in infinity-categories, Lemma 9.8, printed pp.24-25; expanded mapping-space verification of the fiber construction underlying HTT Corollary 4.3.1.11.

proof.text:
The assumed small colimits of the fiber give a colimiting cocone $\nu:D\to\Delta_J L$ in $\mathcal E_b$. In the functor quasicategory, the edges $\lambda:a\to D$ and $\nu:D\to\Delta_J L$ form an inner $2$-horn. The map $p_J$ is an inner fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Its image horn has edges $\beta$ and the identity of $\Delta_J b$. Fill it over the degenerate $2$-simplex with those edges in the base. The third edge is a coherent composite $\mu:a\to\Delta_J L$ with $p_J(\mu)=\beta$; retain this $2$-simplex as the composition witness. We now verify its universal property in the total category. For an arbitrary $y\in\mathcal E$, put $c=p(y)$. Precomposition with $\mu$ gives the top map of the homotopy-commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L,y)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_J y)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,c)&\xrightarrow{\,g\mapsto\Delta_J(g)\beta\,}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal B)}(pa,\Delta_J c).\end{array}$$
The vertical maps are induced by $p$ and the square retains the composition homotopy from the chosen $2$-simplex, whose image under $p_J$ is the specified degenerate base triangle. Its bottom map is an equivalence by the colimit criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applied to $\beta$. All four corners are spaces by the same node.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng-Nikolaus, Lax colimits and free fibrations in infinity-categories, Lemma 9.8, printed pp.24-25; expanded mapping-space verification of the fiber construction underlying HTT Corollary 4.3.1.11.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $g:b\to c$ of the lower left corner of step 2. The $K=\Delta^0$ case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the homotopy fiber of its left vertical map at $g$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_c}(g_!L,y)$. The $K=J$ case identifies the homotopy fiber of its right vertical map at $\Delta_J(g)\beta$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E_c)}(g_!D,\Delta_J y)$. Here the composition clause identifies transport along $\Delta_J(g)\beta$ with successive transport along $\beta$ and $\Delta_J(g)$. Because this identification is compatible with precomposition, the induced map of homotopy fibers is precomposition with the cocone $g_!\nu:g_!D\to\Delta_J(g_!L)$. The hypothesis that every transport preserves small colimits says exactly that this cocone is colimiting. The cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes this map of fibers an equivalence. This holds for every $g$ and for the specified coherent fiber comparison, rather than just for connected components.

source.place: Gepner-Haugseng-Nikolaus, Lax colimits and free fibrations in infinity-categories, Lemma 9.8, printed pp.24-25; expanded mapping-space verification of the fiber construction underlying HTT Corollary 4.3.1.11.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to the square of step 2: its bottom map is an equivalence, its corners are Kan spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and step 3 verifies its homotopy-fiber maps at every vertex of the lower left corner. Thus its top map is an equivalence for every $y$. The dual cone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] implies that $\mu$ is colimiting. Its apex is precisely the fiber colimit $L=\operatorname{colim}_j f_{j,!}a(j)$. The construction works for every small $J$, proving cocompleteness of $\mathcal E$, with the claimed cocone.

proof.text: For the Cartesian assertion pass to $p^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse the diagram shape. Reversing a simplex carries the inner horn $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, so $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$ are quasicategories and $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an inner fibration; reversal also gives isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})$ with the two endpoints exchanged. The right-pinched mapping spaces of $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ are not literally those of $\mathcal C$ with the arguments exchanged; compare them through the arrow mapping spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]: $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\simeq U_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\cong U_{\mathcal C}(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq U_{\mathcal C}(y,x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(y,x)$, where the middle isomorphism is the reversal just described and $Z^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq Z$ for a Kan complex $Z$ because $t\mapsto(t_n,\ldots,t_0)$ on each $|\Delta^n|$ is a homeomorphism $|Z^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|Z|$; these comparisons are natural under the simplicial functors $p$, $p_J$ and $\Delta_J$ by the naturality clause of that node. Hence, with the mapping-space definitions of the statement, Cartesian lifts for $p$ are cocartesian lifts for $p^{\mathrm{op}}$, the fiber of $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $(\mathcal E_b)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the transport along the reversed arrow $f_j^{\mathrm{op}}:pa(j)\to b$ is $(f_j^*)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Likewise the cone category $(\Delta_J\downarrow a)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is, after reversal, the cocone category of $a^{\mathrm{op}}:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and its terminal objects are the initial objects of the reversed category by the same mapping-space comparison; so a limit cone is a colimit cocone after this reversal. Hence completeness of the base and fibers and limit preservation of $f^*$ are exactly the hypotheses of steps 1-4 for $p^{\mathrm{op}}$. Their result reverses to the limiting cone in $\mathcal E$ with apex $\lim_j f_j^*a(j)$ in $\mathcal E_b$, where $b=\lim_Jpa$. Reversal preserves smallness. For the empty shape the constructions take the initial object in the fiber over the base initial object, or the terminal object in the fiber over the base terminal object; the same mapping-space argument applies without a nonemptiness assumption.
